faq.charcount.0.q: Which count do Korean job applications use — with or without spaces?
faq.charcount.0.a: It depends on the company. If the form says “including spaces”, use that number; if it says nothing, including spaces is the usual assumption. Both numbers are shown, so check them together.
faq.charcount.1.q: Why are there two byte counts?
faq.charcount.1.a: In UTF-8 a Korean syllable takes 3 bytes; in EUC-KR it takes 2. Message boards, SMS and database limits are written against one encoding or the other, so both are shown.
faq.charcount.2.q: Does the text I type go anywhere?
faq.charcount.2.a: Nothing is sent to a server — the counting all happens in your browser. It is kept briefly in **this browser’s storage** so a refresh does not lose your work; “Clear” removes it, and it never reaches another device or a server.
faq.charcount.3.q: What is the manuscript-page count based on?
faq.charcount.3.a: The Korean 200-character manuscript sheet (20 boxes per line, 10 lines per sheet). A line break throws away the rest of that line, so the sheet count can be higher than characters ÷ 200 — that is how real sheets fill up.
faq.charcount.4.q: Why do I get a warning when I add an emoji?
faq.charcount.4.a: EUC-KR, the older Korean encoding, cannot hold characters like emoji. If the byte limit you are working against is EUC-KR, pasting them can break or get rejected, so you are told in advance.
faq.charcount.5.q: How is the reading time worked out?
faq.charcount.5.a: It assumes 500 characters a minute reading silently and 300 characters a minute reading aloud, for Korean text. Handy for sizing a script you have to present.
faq.qrgen.0.q: Does the QR code I make expire?
faq.qrgen.0.a: No. The content sits inside the QR itself rather than behind a shortened URL, so it keeps working for as long as the image exists.
faq.qrgen.1.q: Which error-correction level should I pick?
faq.qrgen.1.a: M is plenty for ordinary use. Choose H if you are putting a logo in the middle or printing onto something that may get damaged. The higher the level, the denser the QR.
faq.qrgen.2.q: How do I use the WiFi QR?
faq.qrgen.2.a: Enter the network name (SSID), the password and the security type. Pointing a camera at it connects without typing the password. It works with the stock iOS and Android cameras.
faq.qrgen.3.q: What is the minimum size for printing?
faq.qrgen.3.a: At least 2cm × 2cm in the real world, with a quiet margin of at least four module widths around it. The margin is added for you.
faq.qrgen.4.q: I added a logo and it says it cannot be read.
faq.qrgen.4.a: The logo is covering too many modules. Shrink it, or raise the error correction to H (30%). This tool actually re-reads the QR it made, so keep adjusting until the message turns green.
faq.jsonfmt.0.q: Is it safe to paste an API response in here?
faq.jsonfmt.0.a: Parsing happens only in your browser and nothing is sent to a server. On a shared computer, do clear the box when you are done.
faq.jsonfmt.1.a: Standard JSON does not allow comments, so it is reported as an error. If you use JSONC or JSON5, strip the comments first.
faq.jsonfmt.2.q: How large a JSON can it handle?
faq.jsonfmt.2.a: As large as the browser’s memory allows. A few megabytes is usually fine, but very large files make the display sluggish.
faq.jsonfmt.3.q: What gets copied when I click a line in the tree?
faq.jsonfmt.3.a: The path to that value — something like `$.users[0].name`, which you can paste straight into code, jq or a JSONPath expression.
faq.jsonfmt.4.a: It never changes anything by itself. For common slips — trailing commas, single quotes, comments, unquoted keys — it offers “fix it like this” only when the fixed version actually parses, and you decide whether to take it. Silently rewriting your input would hide what was wrong.
faq.base64.0.q: Why does non-Latin text come out broken?
faq.base64.0.a: The browser’s built-in function works on bytes, so passing text like Hangul straight in throws an error. Here it is encoded as UTF-8 going in and read back as UTF-8, so nothing breaks.
faq.base64.1.q: When do I need the URL-safe form?
faq.base64.1.a: The + and / in Base64 mean other things inside a URL. When the value travels in an address or a token, the - and _ form is used instead. JWTs work this way.
faq.base64.2.a: No. It is just a way of writing bytes down, and anyone can reverse it. If you need something kept secret, encrypt it.
faq.uuidgen.0.q: Should I use v4 or v7?
faq.uuidgen.0.a: v4 is enough for most things. v7 helps where sorting by creation order matters, such as a database primary key — its leading bits are the timestamp, so indexes fragment less.
faq.uuidgen.1.a: UUID v4 carries 122 random bits, so collisions are not a practical concern. Note that v7 exposes the creation time inside the value, so it is a poor fit when that has to stay hidden.
faq.uuidgen.2.q: Can I use the passwords this makes?
faq.uuidgen.2.a: They come from the browser’s cryptographic randomness and are never stored or transmitted. On a shared computer, clear the screen when you are done.
faq.hashgen.0.q: Does the file get uploaded to a server?
faq.hashgen.0.a: No. It is hashed locally with the browser’s WebCrypto, and no data leaves over the network.
faq.hashgen.1.q: Can I store passwords as MD5?
faq.hashgen.1.a: Please don’t. MD5 and SHA-1 have known collisions and should only be used to check integrity. For passwords use a purpose-built algorithm such as bcrypt or argon2.
faq.hashgen.2.q: Does it handle very large files?
faq.hashgen.2.a: The whole file is loaded into memory, so multi-gigabyte files can be too much for a browser. For those, an OS command (certutil, sha256sum) is the better tool.
faq.timer.0.q: Is it accurate while I am looking at another tab?
faq.timer.0.a: Yes. Instead of counting frames it takes the difference between the start time and now, so error does not pile up even when the browser slows a background tab down.
faq.timer.1.a: Browsers block sound until the page has been clicked at least once. If you started it with the Start button it will ring normally. Check that the device is not muted too.
faq.timer.2.q: Will it alert me if I close the window?
faq.timer.2.a: No — the tab has to stay open. If you need an alarm that wakes a sleeping computer, use the Alarm tool in the KarmoLab desktop app.
faq.datecalc.0.a: If the birthday has passed it is (this year − birth year); if not, one less. Since June 2023 this so-called “full age” is the single legal age in Korea.
faq.datecalc.1.q: Is the target day D-0 or D-1?
faq.datecalc.1.a: Here the target day itself is D-DAY and the day before is D-1. Places that follow a different convention can be one day off.
faq.datecalc.2.q: Are public holidays taken out of the business-day count?
faq.datecalc.2.a: Only Saturdays and Sundays are removed. Public holidays move from year to year and are not included, so subtract them yourself if you need to.
faq.unitconv.0.q: How many square metres is one Korean pyeong?
faq.unitconv.0.a: One pyeong is about 3.3058m². The other way round, 1m² is about 0.3025 pyeong.
faq.unitconv.1.q: Is data size based on 1000 or 1024?
faq.unitconv.1.a: The binary basis, where 1KB = 1024B. Storage manufacturers label their products on the 1000 basis, so the numbers can differ.
faq.unitconv.2.q: How many grams is one Korean geun?
faq.unitconv.2.a: It is worked out here as 600g. In practice meat uses 600g while vegetables and fruit use 375g, so it depends on the item.
faq.unitconv.3.q: How is the price per pyeong worked out?
faq.unitconv.3.a: The area above is converted to pyeong and the total is divided by it. For example 84m² (25.41 pyeong) at 600 million won is about 23.6 million won per pyeong, or about 7.14 million per m². Whether you entered the gross or the net floor area is for you to check.
faq.textdiff.0.q: Does it show characters that changed inside a line?
faq.textdiff.0.a: Comparison is by line at the moment. If a single character differs, that whole line shows as added and removed.
faq.textdiff.1.q: How long can the texts be?
faq.textdiff.1.a: Up to 2,000 lines each. Beyond that it compares the beginning and tells you it was cut. The limit is there because the diff algorithm can freeze a browser on very long input.
faq.textdiff.2.q: Can I use it for code?
faq.textdiff.2.a: Yes. It uses a monospace font and shows line numbers on both sides. There is no syntax highlighting though.
faq.textdiff.3.q: Can I see only the part that changed within a line?
faq.textdiff.3.a: Yes. When an added line follows a removed one, it is treated as “one line rewritten” and only the differing characters are shown in bold. Korean has few spaces, so splitting by word would make the whole line look changed — it works character by character.
faq.regextest.0.q: Which regex flavour does it use?
faq.regextest.0.a: The browser’s own JavaScript (ECMAScript) engine. Syntax specific to Python or PCRE will not work.
faq.regextest.1.a: g searches the whole string, i ignores case, m makes ^ and $ work per line, s lets . match newlines, and u turns on Unicode handling.
faq.regextest.2.q: Are there patterns that freeze the browser?
faq.regextest.2.a: Nested repetition such as (a+)+b can slow down sharply on certain input. Matching stops at 5,000 hits here, but patterns like that are dangerous in production too, so they are best avoided.
faq.colorconv.0.q: What does a contrast ratio of 4.5:1 mean?
faq.colorconv.0.a: It is the minimum contrast the WCAG accessibility guidelines ask for on body text. 4.5 or more meets AA, 7 or more meets AAA, and text at 18pt and above passes at 3:1.
faq.colorconv.1.q: The CMYK values differ from what my printer says.
faq.colorconv.1.a: Screens (RGB) and print (CMYK) cover different ranges, and an accurate conversion needs a colour profile. The values here are a profile-less approximation, so use professional tools for print proofing.
faq.colorconv.2.q: How is the harmony palette built?
faq.colorconv.2.a: By rotating the angle on the HSL colour wheel: 180° for the complement, 120° and 240° for the triad, and ±30° for the analogous colours.
faq.asciiart.0.q: Does the image get uploaded to a server?
faq.asciiart.0.a: No. It is read and processed on a browser canvas, and no data leaves over the network.
faq.asciiart.1.a: Monospace characters are taller than they are wide. That ratio is corrected automatically, but wide line spacing where you paste it can stretch it again. Keep the line height near 1.0.
faq.asciiart.2.a: Images with strong contrast and a simple background. For people, cropping tightly to the face reads much better.
faq.asciiart.3.a: “Add colour” is for the on-screen preview only. Copying the text or saving the PNG gives you a single colour.
faq.specialchar.0.q: It shows as a box (□) when I paste it.
faq.specialchar.0.a: The font does not carry that character. Use a different font, or pick a character with wider support.
faq.specialchar.1.q: Can I type special characters from a Korean keyboard?
faq.specialchar.1.a: Press a consonant such as ㅁ, ㅂ or ㅅ and then the Hanja key to get a list. That list is small though, so this table is faster.
faq.specialchar.2.q: What is the value starting with U+?
faq.specialchar.2.a: The Unicode code point. You use it for \u escapes in code or as an HTML numeric reference.
faq.ascii.0.q: What is the difference between ASCII and Unicode?
faq.ascii.0.a: ASCII is an early standard that defines only 128 characters; Unicode contains those same 128 and adds the writing systems of the world. In UTF-8 the ASCII range is still one byte.
faq.ascii.1.q: Is keyCode the same value as the ASCII code?
faq.ascii.1.a: No. The keyCode on a keyboard event is based on key position, so it can disagree with the character code. If you need the key itself, use the keyboard event code table.
faq.ascii.2.a: 128–255 is called extended ASCII, but there is no single standard for it — it differs by environment. Only the standard range is listed here to avoid the confusion.
faq.htmlentity.0.q: Can I not just write the character directly?
faq.htmlentity.0.a: In a UTF-8 document you usually can. But <, > and & clash with the markup itself, so those must be written as entities.
faq.htmlentity.1.a: Where a line must not break — between a number and its unit, for example. Using several in a row to push things apart is a job for CSS instead.
faq.htmlentity.2.q: What are the numeric ones like ₩?
faq.htmlentity.2.a: A way of naming a character by its Unicode number. You use it when the character has no named entity.
faq.httpstatus.0.q: What is the difference between 401 and 403?
faq.httpstatus.0.a: 401 means “I do not know who you are” — you need to sign in. 403 means “I know who you are, and you are not allowed”.
faq.httpstatus.1.a: Use 301 when the address has moved permanently; search engines carry the ranking over to the new one. For something temporary, use 302 or 307.
faq.httpstatus.2.q: What is the difference between 404 and 410?
faq.httpstatus.2.a: 404 means “not here right now”, 410 means “gone for good”. Returning 410 gets it dropped from the index faster.
faq.colorname.0.q: Is it fine to use colour names directly?
faq.colorname.0.a: Every browser supports them, so yes. Inside a design system, though, variables that carry meaning are easier to maintain.
faq.colorname.1.q: Do both gray and grey work?
faq.colorname.1.a: Both are valid. This table lists the gray spelling.
faq.colorname.2.q: Where do the exact HEX values come from?
faq.colorname.2.a: They are asked of the browser itself. Nothing was copied by hand, so there are no typos.
faq.keycode.0.q: Should I use key or code?
faq.keycode.0.a: Use key when the character typed is what matters, and code when the physical key position matters (WASD movement and the like). code stays the same across keyboard layouts.
faq.keycode.1.a: It is deprecated in the standard. Refer to it only when maintaining old code; use key and code for anything new.
faq.keycode.2.a: Keys like F5 and Ctrl+W are taken by the browser first. A web page cannot intercept those.
faq.radix.0.q: Is it accurate for very large numbers?
faq.radix.0.a: Yes. It calculates with BigInt, so the value stays exact no matter how many digits there are — none of the rounding error you get from ordinary floating point.
faq.radix.1.a: Put a minus sign in front. It is written as a sign plus a magnitude, not as two’s complement.
faq.radix.2.q: Why is the binary broken into groups of four?
faq.radix.2.a: Four binary digits map exactly onto one hexadecimal digit, so grouping them makes it easy to line the two up by eye.
faq.textclean.0.q: In what order are the steps applied?
faq.textclean.0.a: Fixed: tidy whitespace → drop blank lines → remove duplicates → sort → change case → prefix and suffix → number the lines. Toggling a checkbox lets you compare the result immediately.
faq.textclean.1.a: Yes — it uses the Korean collation rules. Mixed with Latin text, each is placed by its own language rules.
faq.textclean.2.q: Does the text get sent to a server?
faq.textclean.2.a: No. Everything happens inside your browser and what you type is never sent anywhere.
faq.emoji.0.q: Why does searching in English sometimes miss things?
faq.emoji.0.a: The official emoji names are English but often unhelpful — “face with tears of joy” is not what anyone types. Extra search words are attached to each entry so everyday wording finds them.
faq.emoji.1.q: The emoji shows as a box.
faq.emoji.1.a: The device or browser has no font for it. The copied value itself is fine, so it will show properly wherever the font exists.
faq.emoji.2.q: Why do they look different on different devices?
faq.emoji.2.a: Emoji are characters, not pictures — Apple, Google, Samsung and others each draw their own font. The same character can look quite different.
faq.markdown.0.a: GitHub Flavored Markdown, the dialect GitHub uses. Tables, checkboxes and strikethrough — none of which were in the original Markdown — were added there.
faq.markdown.1.q: I copied it and it did not work.
faq.markdown.1.a: Support for tables, checkboxes and collapsible sections varies from editor to editor. Each entry notes where it works.
faq.markdown.2.q: How do I write a literal asterisk?
faq.markdown.2.a: Put a backslash in front of it. There is an escaping entry under “common snags”.
faq.percent.0.q: Why a row of sentences instead of one calculator?
faq.percent.0.a: Percentage questions use a different formula depending on which way round you ask. A single set of boxes leaves you guessing what goes where, so each question is written out as its own line.
faq.percent.1.q: Why do the increase and decrease not match?
faq.percent.1.a: 100 raised by 20% is 120, but getting from 120 back to 100 takes about 16.7% off, not 20% — because the number you measure against has changed.
faq.percent.2.q: Where do I calculate a price after a discount?
faq.percent.2.a: Use the “take N% off” line. For adding something on, like tax, use the “add N%” line.
faq.palette.0.q: Does the image get uploaded to a server?
faq.palette.0.a: No. It is read and processed entirely inside your browser and never transmitted anywhere.
faq.palette.1.a: By median cut — repeatedly splitting the colour cloud in half along its widest axis. Unlike simply counting the most frequent colours, an accent colour surrounded by a large background still survives.
faq.palette.2.q: Can I paste a screenshot straight in?
faq.palette.2.a: Yes. Copy your screen, paste it over this tool, and the palette appears right away.
faq.urlparse.0.q: Why do things like %EC appear in a URL?
faq.urlparse.0.a: A URL may only carry Latin letters, digits and a few symbols, so anything else — non-Latin letters, spaces — is rewritten in a fixed way. That rewriting is what %EC looks like.
faq.urlparse.1.q: Is it safe to remove tracking parameters?
faq.urlparse.1.a: Yes. Values like utm_source and fbclid exist to record where you clicked from, and the link goes to the same page without them. Stripping them makes a shared link tidier.
faq.urlparse.2.q: Does it work on text that is not a URL?
faq.urlparse.2.a: Encoding and decoding do. Splitting into parameters only works on a complete address starting with http://.
faq.gitcmd.0.q: Why is it organised by situation rather than command name?
faq.gitcmd.0.a: In git the name and the job rarely match. reset, revert and restore cannot be told apart by name — but ask “what do I want to undo” and only one answer fits.
faq.gitcmd.1.q: What is the difference between reset and revert?
faq.gitcmd.1.a: reset makes the commit as if it never happened; revert adds a new commit that undoes it. On a branch you share with others, revert is safer because it leaves history alone.
faq.gitcmd.2.q: I lost a commit by mistake.
faq.gitcmd.2.a: `git reflog` lists the commits you have recently been on. Find the hash there and go back to it — that usually recovers it.
faq.filetype.0.q: Does renaming the extension change the file format?
faq.filetype.0.a: No. Only the label changes; the contents stay as they were. Renaming a jpg to png leaves it a jpg, and some programs will refuse to open it. Use a converter instead.
faq.filetype.1.q: Is it safe to open a file I do not recognise?
faq.filetype.1.a: Anything executable — exe, apk, sh, ps1 — should not be opened when you do not know where it came from. Documents and images are usually safe, though older formats can carry vulnerabilities.
faq.filetype.2.q: My CSV opens with broken characters in Excel.
faq.filetype.2.a: The file’s encoding and the one Excel assumes do not match. Open it through Excel’s data-import step and choose UTF-8 there.
faq.shortcut.0.q: Why is this not the full list?
faq.shortcut.0.a: People open a shortcut table to find something they did not know, not to confirm what they already do. A full dump is harder to read, so only the ones you would actually reach for are kept.
faq.shortcut.1.q: What do I press instead of Ctrl on a Mac?
faq.shortcut.1.a: Command, mostly. Terminals and developer tools sometimes keep Ctrl as it is, so each entry says which one it means.
faq.shortcut.2.q: Can I reopen a tab I closed by accident?
faq.shortcut.2.a: Ctrl (Cmd) + Shift + T. Press it repeatedly and the tabs come back in order, going further into the past.
faq.caseconv.0.q: Does it handle names like XMLHttpRequest?
faq.caseconv.0.a: Yes. When a new word starts after a run of capitals, it splits there — XML · Http · Request.
faq.caseconv.1.q: Which style should I use where?
faq.caseconv.1.a: Usually camelCase for JavaScript variables, PascalCase for classes and components, snake_case for Python and database columns, kebab-case for URLs and CSS classes, and SCREAMING_SNAKE for constants and environment variables.
faq.caseconv.2.q: What about names in scripts without letter case?
faq.caseconv.2.a: Parts separated by spaces, underscores or hyphens are still split — but writing systems without upper and lower case (Hangul, kana, Han) gain little from a case conversion.
faq.jwt.0.q: Is it safe to paste a JWT in here?
faq.jwt.0.a: This tool decodes it inside your browser and sends it nowhere. But a JWT is signed plain text, not encryption — if the token itself leaks, anyone can read it and use it as is. Never paste a live token into a random site.
faq.jwt.1.q: Why does it not verify the signature?
faq.jwt.1.a: Verifying needs the secret or public key. Making people paste a secret key into a web page is itself dangerous, so it was deliberately left out.
faq.jwt.2.q: What do exp, iat and sub mean?
faq.jwt.2.a: exp is the expiry time, iat the issue time, and sub the subject the token refers to (usually the user ID). The times are seconds since 1970, so a human-readable time is shown alongside.
faq.cron.0.q: Why show the next run times as well?
faq.cron.0.a: A description still has to be interpreted; a time is simply right or wrong. If the time you expected does not appear, the expression is wrong and you see it immediately.
faq.cron.1.q: What happens if I set both day-of-month and day-of-week?
faq.cron.1.a: In standard cron it runs when *either* matches (OR). Setting the 1st and Monday together means it runs on the 1st of every month and on every Monday.
faq.cron.2.a: This handles the standard five fields (minute hour day month weekday) only. Six-field notation with seconds is an extension that only some programs use.
faq.lotto.0.a: No. Each Korean 6/45 draw is independent, so no condition can change the probability. It only saves you the work of picking numbers.
faq.lotto.1.a: Six distinct numbers from the browser’s randomness. It redraws until your conditions are met, and tells you if it gave up and drew without them.
faq.lotto.2.q: Why is there an odd/even balance option?
faq.lotto.2.a: Winning combinations often land between 2:4 and 4:2 odd to even. There is no probabilistic advantage — it is there for when you want that shape.
faq.ladder.0.q: Is the outcome decided in advance?
faq.ladder.0.a: No. The ladder is drawn at random first and shown on screen, then the path is actually walked down it. You can follow the drawn ladder yourself and check the result.
faq.ladder.1.a: From two to ten. Fewer and there is no ladder to speak of; more and the paths become hard to follow on a narrow screen.
faq.ladder.2.q: What if I leave the outcomes empty?
faq.ladder.2.a: It builds a default board where only the first line wins and the rest do not.
